topics.topic: Concrete backup polling cadence and initial polling offset
questions: What concrete polling cadence should generated code use once the first-look rule and maximum permitted gap are fixed?
What concrete polling cadence and initial polling offset should the generated process use while preserving the maximum-gap guarantee?

quotes:
The process looks at the clock at least once in each interval of
   the imported `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` constant (60 seconds);
judgement.why: P1 already judged the same cadence and initial-offset question on unchanged passages, finding that State 5 fixes a process-start-anchored monotonic cadence with the first look one interval after serving begins.
options: Use monotonic deadlines from serving start, first look after one interval, counting suspension and making one late call after resume.
Look immediately at process start.
Schedule relative to each preceding look or its completion.
Use UTC wall-clock cadence.
consequences: The later text selects the first option; a process starting after the last pre-03:00 deadline may have no qualifying earlier look, and missed deadlines are not replayed.

topics.topic: Meaning of the variables, inequality, and length measurement in the formal secret invariant

quotes:
A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at
   least the imported `SECRET_MIN_BYTES` constant (32, SPEC_STANDARD §15.3.1)
   of bytes in UTF-8 long; a shorter one fails the start.

For each kind of secret — a service
   token, the owner credential and the backup key — a value one byte shorter
   than `SECRET_MIN_BYTES` stops the start and one of exactly
   `SECRET_MIN_BYTES` bytes is accepted. The length is counted in UTF-8
   bytes, not characters: a token of 16 two-byte characters (32 bytes) is
   accepted, and one of 15 two-byte characters and one one-byte character
   (31 bytes) stops the start.
judgement.why: The normative rule and required test expressly apply the minimum to every configured secret and define length as UTF-8 bytes, so the invariant's `len` cannot denote only one unspecified member of a pair.
options: State the length condition separately for every configured secret.
Apply the same per-secret condition to both members when expressing it inside each distinct-field pair.
consequences: Either faithful formulation requires every configured secret value to contain at least `SECRET_MIN_BYTES` UTF-8 bytes.
